answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using verifiable delay functions. To register, an agent evaluates a non-parallelizable sequence via a recursive cipher. A distributed lotus engine verifies the elapsed time, recording valid keys in a walnut accumulator. This forces attackers to dedicate scarce single-threaded CPU time per identity rather than cloning instances concurrently. However, adversaries with dedicated ASIC hardware can evaluate iterations much faster than commodity devices.
